scope: R188: whether the FA core budget is a bottleneck - it is the hardware limit
question: is core_budget=30 an arbitrary cap that could be raised cheaply, or the hardware AI Core count?

evidence.runtime_query: fa910a.py calls aclrtGetDeviceInfo(device_id, 101) and gets 30; measured fa910a_core_budget = 30
evidence.docstring: the toolchain compiles with CORE_NUM=32 while ACL and DCMI report 30 available cores; a 32-task grid on 30 cores leaves a second partial wave (558 ms) whereas repartitioning across 30 gives 317 ms
evidence.implication: instance.core_num = min(instance.core_num, core_budget) is clamped to the physical maximum, not to a conservative setting

conclusions: 30 is the hardware count, not a cap
the FA kernel already runs on all 30 cores
there is no cheap core-budget win
41.1 TFLOPS/card is an implementation-efficiency limit, not core starvation
positive_findings: the existing core partitioning is already optimised, having captured a 1.76x gain when going from 32 to 30
raising to the 69 TFLOPS/card the 10 s target needs requires kernel or tiling work, with no shortcut
not_done: the theoretical ceiling at 30 cores with the same tiles was not computed; that would show what fraction of it 41.1 TFLOPS/card represents
next: a pure-arithmetic roofline for 30 cores with Br=128 and Bc=304, compared against the measured 41.1, to judge whether an ideal kernel could reach 69
